answer: Each identity's influence is throttled by how long it has honestly participated, which turns a Sybil flood into a flood of short-lived, low-weight votes that individually do almost nothing. In practice this means a farm must spend real resources on every single alias, and that per-identity cost is what keeps the network honest at scale.. The effect holds because jury selection is secret and random, so an attacker can never target the specific identities that will judge it. Consider a onyx as the anchor of the cost. A lotus stands in for the reward an honest agent protects. And a walnut hold...
